title: The Locker of Route 9
premise: Emrys Sterling, a nonbinary baker's kid who channels feelings into bread, has survived high school by staying invisible — until a college essay prompt ('What truth have you kept to survive?') is accidentally posted publicly, and Emrys's anonymous answer goes viral. As classmates recognize themselves in the confession and begin unmasking each other's secrets, Emrys must choose between protecting their best friend Priya's secret or their own hard-won authenticity. At prom, with the labels stripped away, Emrys claims their name publicly, loses the friendship they tried to preserve by silence, and discovers that belonging built on hiding was never belonging at all.
about_author: Hazel Dunmore is the pen name of a former small-town bakery counter worker who writes stories about quiet kids with loud interiors. They live somewhere with unreliable weather and a sourdough starter named after a minor literary character.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. We meet them at 4 a.m. in the family bakery, kneading anxiety into a batch of rye for a teacher they resent. Establishes the bread-as-feeling magic realism, their invisibility strategy at Route 9 High, and the college essay deadline looming. Emotional beat: the ache of being carefully unseen.

chapters.title: The Prompt
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. English class receives the essay prompt: 'What truth have you kept to survive?' Emrys drafts an honest answer at midnight and submits it to the wrong portal — one that publishes anonymously to the whole school. Beat: dread blooming like overproofed dough.

chapters.title: Viral Crumbs
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Emrys and Priya. The essay spreads; students start answering it themselves on a shared doc, trading secrets. Priya defends the anonymity fiercely — too fiercely. Emrys realizes Priya may be hiding something of her own. Beat: intoxicating connection shadowed by fear.

chapters.title: What the Rye Knew
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A classmate, Theo, correctly guesses the essay is Emrys's from its rhythm and keeps the secret — becoming an unexpected ally and crush. Meanwhile Emrys bakes 'confession loaves' that make eaters briefly honest, causing a cafeteria incident. Beat: warmth, first flirtation, rising stakes.

chapters.title: Labels
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The shared doc turns cruel as students weaponize each other's truths. Priya's own secret — her undocumented status and fear of the essay trail leading to her family — surfaces to Emrys alone. She begs Emrys to help bury the thread. Beat: loyalty pulling against conscience.

chapters.title: The Long Rise
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys helps Priya scrub the doc but deletes a classmate's vulnerable post in the process, gutting them. Theo confronts Emrys about complicity: 'You can't proof everyone else's life and never bake your own.' Beat: guilt, self-betrayal recognized.

chapters.title: Sourdough
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The school suspends the essay assignment; a beloved teacher takes the fall for the leak, and Emrys knows the real source was their own mistake. Priya asks Emrys to stay silent. Emrys bakes nothing at all for the first time. Beat: the cost of protection made tangible.

chapters.title: Scoring
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Before prom, Emrys confesses to the teacher privately and then, in front of the senior assembly, reads the essay aloud under their own name — including the parts about gender, hunger, and hiding. The room splits; Priya walks out. Beat: climax — truth chosen over safety.

chapters.title: Prom, Unlabeled
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At prom, Emrys arrives without a mask or a title, dances badly, and rebuilds bridges one honest conversation at a time. Priya appears at the end; she isn't ready to forgive, but she brings Emrys's forgotten jacket — a door left open. Beat: tender, unresolved hope.

chapters.title: Day-Old Bread
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Graduation week: the teacher returns, Priya and Emrys share a careful, changed friendship, and Emrys submits the final college essay — signed. In the bakery, they teach a younger kid to knead. Beat: resolution — belonging earned, not performed; survival redefined as living.
